summary:
The Comunitat Valenciana has its own two-statute framework for trans and LGTBI people: Ley 8/2017 of 7 April, the integral law on the right to gender identity and expression, and Ley 23/2018 of 29 November on LGTBI equality. Both sit under the Spanish national framework on legal gender recognition carried by the national record; what follows is the regional layer.

Article 1 of Ley 8/2017 sets the law's purpose as guaranteeing an adequate normative framework for gender self-determination for people whose felt gender identity differs from that assigned at birth, and public bodies of the Comunitat Valenciana must treat people according to their felt gender identity. The duty reaches the regional administration, health and education services a visitor may deal with.

Ley 23/2018 prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, provides access and admission rights (article 56), reverses the burden of proof (article 57), and establishes a Title V regime of administrative infringements and sanctions for discrimination against LGTBI people (articles 58 to 66). A complaint about being refused service or admission in the region can shift the evidential burden onto the respondent, and the regional administration can fine discriminators.

Regional courts have handled gender-identity-motivated offences. The Audiencia Provincial de Valencia, Section 5, convicted over a June 2022 incident in a Valencia park in Patraix, where an 18-year-old and several minors insulted, chased, filmed and mocked a trans woman solely because of her gender identity. The adult accepted six months' imprisonment, suspended for two years on condition of committing no offence, plus a 720-euro fine and 1,000 euros in moral damages to the victim; two minors had already been sentenced to supervision measures. The specialised hate-crime prosecutor (fiscal coordinadora de delitos de odio) handled the case.
tangentialFactors: The inventory of regional gender-identity laws lists two statutes for the Comunitat Valenciana where most of the autonomous communities it covers list one. Protection in the region therefore rests on a trans-specific law plus a general LGTBI equality law, with administrative sanctions available where discrimination is proved.
localsOnly:
Title III of Ley 8/2017 provides for administrative documentation and an advice and support service for trans people and their families, administered within the Comunitat Valenciana.

The LGTBI federation's 2025 radiography of public education policies across Spain's autonomous communities places the Comunitat Valenciana among the communities with the fullest coverage of gender-identity protocols and education legislation, and records that the Valencian parliament completed its gender legislation.
outOfScopeNotes:
Consulted sources contain no regional aggregate of hate-crime complaints or convictions for the Comunitat Valenciana, so the single Valencia prosecution cannot be read as a rate or as a trend.

The assessment of education policy is a civil-society federation review published in 2025, not an official audit.

The inventory records no amendment or repeal of Ley 8/2017 or Ley 23/2018, and does not establish how the duty on public bodies to treat people by felt gender identity is applied in practice beyond the prosecuted case above. Both statutes are published in the Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE-A-2017-5118 and BOE-A-2019-281).
